summary: Traffic surge causes canary routing to bypass model-version pin for certain sessions
description:
Issue summary: During a large QPS spike for NovaChat, a subset of requests that had been explicitly pinned to rw-instruct-3b-v2 began receiving responses from the canary variant (rw-instruct-3b-v2-canary).

Impact: Customer reported inconsistent outputs (semantically different completions) for user sessions pinned to a stable model version. This impacted a small percentage (~3-5%) of requests over a 20 minute window, causing visible UX regressions for high-value enterprise customers.

Environment: Production (us-east). Customer uses Dedicated cluster with reserved capacity and a model-version pin configured at the route-level via the Console and API.

Observed behaviour: Pin set in route configuration appears to have been ignored for some requests; those requests were routed to canary. Canary traffic was permitted by rollout policy, but pinned sessions were expected to be excluded.

Expected behaviour: Requests from sessions pinned to rw-instruct-3b-v2 should consistently route to that exact model variant until pin is removed or updated. Policy-based canary rollouts must not override explicit pins.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer creates route and pins to rw-instruct-3b-v2 using Console -> Routes -> Advanced -> Pin model to v2
2) Customer issues sustained requests at ~1200 QPS for 15-30 minutes from multiple clients (simulates production surge),
3) Observe routing traces for pinned session IDs via support endpoint /v1/traces and in Datadog request logs
4) Check routing decisions — many show selected_variant=rw-instruct-3b-v2-canary while request.headers included x-redwood-pin=rw-instruct-3b-v2
5) Confirm that route table change events and autoscaler provisioning happened during the same window.
logs: trace_id=01F8Z2YQ9J6K8A3B2C7D - routing-decision: candidate_pool=[rw-instruct-3b-v2, rw-instruct-3b-v2-canary] - selected=rw-instruct-3b-v2-canary - reason=canary_policy_eval - pin_header_present=true
autoscaler: scale_event id=scale-993 - spawned router=router-21 - router-21 config_sync_time=2026-02-20T14:04:12Z
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: prefix cache TTL or route cache invalidation allowed new routing instances (router-21) to load a default rollout policy that included the canary variant and did not yet have the pinned-state applied.
Observations from traces: requests that hit router instances created within 120s of the autoscaler event are overrepresented in misroutes.

Config propagation check: Agent confirms that route pin state is stored in the config service and pushed as a delta. Router startup subscribes to config channel; first config snapshot contains rollout settings but an edge-case race can mark pin state as 'pending' until an acknowledgement completes.
Datadog dashboard: increased 5xxs not observed; error rate remained low. The issue is policy-level misrouting rather than infrastructure failures.
Reproduced in staging by simulating route pin + rapid router churn; reproducer attached as runbook steps.
comments: Customer (NovaChat): 'Pin was set at 2026-02-20T13:58Z; we saw odd completions starting ~14:02Z. Roughly 3% of traffic returned canary-style outputs.'
Support (Ava): 'Thanks — collecting traces and routing logs. Can you also provide an example request id and the session id?'
SRE (Diego): 'Found correlation with autoscaler spawn events at 14:03Z. Router-21 accepted traffic before config ack completed. Will instrument config ack path.'
Eng (Routing lead, Priya Rao): 'Adding high-priority patch to ensure strict application of explicit pins at decision-time even if config state is still reconciling. Preparing PR and canary.'
Customer (NovaChat): 'We applied a temporary header-based workaround (x-redwood-strict-pin: true) and saw misroutes drop to near 0.'
resolution_notes: Temporary mitigation: advised customer to set x-redwood-strict-pin: true on requests and increased route sync aggressive backoff for the customer's Dedicated cluster to reduce config reconcilation latency. Long-term fix: merged PR to routing service to enforce pin precedence at decision time and to wait (with a short blocking window) for pin-state on newly started router instances. Patch deployed to canary on 2026-02-21 and promoted to prod us-east on 2026-02-22 between 03:00-03:15 UTC. Post-deploy monitoring showed misroutes drop from ~3-5% to <0.1%. Follow-ups: add a unit test for router startup path, expand integration tests for pin/canary interplay, and update the Canary Routing Runbook with checklist to avoid config-race during autoscaling.
next_steps: 1) SRE to add an observability alert that surfaces pin-sync lag > 5s during autoscaler events (owner: Diego).
2) Routing team to add integration test that simulates route pin and rapid router churn (owner: Priya).
3) Customer success to review Dedicated cluster sync settings with NovaChat and recommend best practices for scheduled high-QPS windows (owner: Mateo).
4) Close follow-up ticket to track runbook update (INT-4199).
